topic: In which country are the Southern Alps? (New Zealand)
policy_note: Every spoken or shown fact → a claim with ≥ 2 independent publishers; core claims need a primary/scholarly source.

wiki_southern_alps.title: Southern Alps
wiki_southern_alps.notes: mountain range along much of the length of New Zealand's South Island; runs approximately 500 km NE–SW; uplift continues on the Alpine Fault

britannica_southern_alps.title: Southern Alps / Kā Tiritiri o te Moana
britannica_southern_alps.notes: range on South Island, New Zealand, extending NE–SW along the island; highest point Aoraki/Mount Cook, 3,724 m

wiki_aoraki.title: Aoraki / Mount Cook
wiki_aoraki.notes: highest mountain in New Zealand; height listed as 3,724 m since 2014 (after the 1991 rock fall and later erosion); in the Southern Alps, South Island

doc_aoraki.title: Aoraki/Mount Cook National Park
doc_aoraki.notes: 'At 3,724 m, New Zealand's tallest peak is known as Aoraki by Māori'; South Island; Tasman Glacier

wiki_south_island.title: South Island
wiki_south_island.notes: divided along its length by the Southern Alps; Aoraki / Mount Cook 3,724 m; the Southern Alps include sixteen other points exceeding 3,000 m (→ 17 peaks over 3,000 m)

wiki_alpine_fault.title: Alpine Fault
wiki_alpine_fault.notes: about 600 km long along the South Island; boundary between the Pacific plate and the Australian plate; the Southern Alps have been uplifted on the fault over the last 12 million years

gns_alpine_fault.publisher: GNS Science (New Zealand Crown Research Institute)
gns_alpine_fault.title: Alpine Fault
gns_alpine_fault.notes: the Alpine Fault is the on-land boundary of the Australian and Pacific plates along the South Island's West Coast

wiki_tasman.title: Tasman Glacier
wiki_tasman.notes: largest glacier in New Zealand; flows from the Southern Alps towards the Mackenzie Basin

wiki_kosciuszko.title: Mount Kosciuszko
wiki_kosciuszko.notes: 2,228 m, highest mountain on mainland Australia

claims.text: The Southern Alps are the mountain range running along the length of New Zealand's South Island, roughly 500 km NE–SW (Britannica gives about 480 km). The Southern Alps are in New Zealand, not Europe.
vo: a range called the alps… nowhere near europe
it's new zealand: the southern alps run five hundred kilometres down the south island
screen: of peaks down the South Island
In which country are the SOUTHERN ALPS?

claims.text: Aoraki / Mount Cook, 3,724 m, is New Zealand's highest mountain (height revised in 2014 after the 1991 collapse and later erosion). Australia's highest peak, Mount Kosciuszko, is 2,228 m, so Aoraki is taller than any Australian mountain.
vo: highest: aoraki, mount cook, three thousand seven hundred and twenty-four metres
screen: Aoraki, the roof of New Zealand

claims.text: The Tasman Glacier is New Zealand's largest and longest glacier — about 23 km long (DOC: 23 km long, up to 3 km wide, 101 km²). Tasman Lake, the proglacial lake at its terminus, did not exist before the 1970s (DOC: formed from small meltwater ponds in the early 1970s).
vo: the tasman glacier, its longest, runs twenty-three kilometres
into a lake that did not exist in 1970

claims.text: The range is uplifted along the Alpine Fault, the boundary between the Pacific and Australian tectonic plates. Uplift along the fault continues today (GNS Science: the Southern Alps are still rising).
vo: it all rides the alpine fault, where the pacific and australian plates collide

myths.reality: New Zealand's Southern Alps are higher than any Australian peak and carry hundreds of glaciers.

guardrails.why: Contested name — say 'the Gulf' or use both names (docs/BORDER_POLICY.md).
Sovereignty language on disputed areas is banned; say administers / claims.

landscape.our_gap: Feed quizzes answer 'New Zealand' over stock peaks; nobody draws the range down the island, drops the 3,724 m pin and then draws the fault that built it.
